nodes.label: fortnox_base_v2_invoices
nodes.dbt_description: One row per Fortnox invoice as delivered by the v2 API, filtered to the tenant's configured start year. Ephemeral, and deliberately named `base_` rather than `_staging`: it applies that year filter once for the five staging models that read it, instead of each repeating it. It does not rename or cast — that stays in the staging models downstream.

nodes.label: fortnox_erp_bi_dim_stockpoints
nodes.dbt_description: One row per Fortnox stock point. Adapts the Fortnox stock point to the common unified schema so `erp_bi_dim_stockpoints` can union it alongside other connectors; its column list and order are the conformed contract, not Fortnox's own shape.

nodes.label: fortnox_erp_bi_fact_attendance_transactions
nodes.dbt_description:
One row per row of `fortnox_api.attendance_transactions` — hours reported against a cause code, with the employee's cost centre and project filled in where the transaction states none of its own.
Grain assumption, untested: `public.cause_codes` is joined on `Code` alone, without `OrgId`, and `fortnox_api.employees` on `(OrgId, EmployeeId)`. Neither is declared unique anywhere in this project, so a duplicate on either side multiplies the transaction and every `Hours` total silently doubles. No column of this model is a key, so the grain cannot be asserted with dbt's built-in tests, and `dbt_utils` — whose `unique_combination_of_columns` and `equal_rowcount` would — is not installed here.

nodes.label: fortnox_erp_bi_fact_salary_transactions
nodes.dbt_description:
One row per row of `fortnox_api.salary_transactions` — one salary line, with the expense's account resolved through the financial year that contains the line's date.
Grain assumption, untested, and weaker than the other fact models here: `financial_years` is joined on `st.Date between fy.FromDate and fy.ToDate`, a range join rather than an equality lookup, so two financial years overlapping for one `OrgId` multiply the line — and `Total`, `VAT` and `NumberOfUnits` with it. The `expenses`, `accounts` and `employees` joins are equality lookups on their natural keys, none of which is declared unique in this project either. No column of this model is a key, so nothing here can assert the grain with dbt's built-in tests.

nodes.label: fortnox_erp_bi_fact_stockbalance
nodes.dbt_description:
One row per row of `fortnox_api.stockbalance` in the most recent snapshot only — one item per stock point, at current balance. The upstream `where` keeps rows whose `ifnull(enz_sync_ts, enz_created_at)` equals the table maximum, so this model carries no history: an earlier balance is not here to be found. There is no join and no unnest, so the grain is exactly the surviving source rows'.
`Date` is `date(ENZ_SYNC_TS)` while the snapshot filter falls back to `enz_created_at`, so a row that survives on the fallback carries a null `Date`. `ItemId` repeats once per stock point and is not a key.

nodes.label: fortnox_erp_bi_fact_stocktakings
nodes.dbt_description:
One row per element of the source's `Rows` array — **not** one per stocktaking. The upstream cross-joins each record to its lines with `unnest(json_extract_array(s.Rows))`, so `StockTakingId`, `Name`, `Date`, `ResponsiblePerson` and `Status` repeat once per counted article. Counting rows here counts article counts, not stocktakings, and `StockTakingId` is deliberately not unique.
`StockTakenQuantity` and `TotalQuantityInStock` are read out of the array element, so they are at this grain and are the columns that may be summed. `stockpoints` is left-joined on `(Id, OrgId)`, which is not declared unique — a duplicate there multiplies the line again.

nodes.label: hubspot_erp_bi_dim_company
nodes.dbt_description: One row per tenant — the organisation whose warehouse this is, read from the tenant's own HubSpot account record. NOT a customer dimension: HubSpot companies are customer organisations and belong in hubspot_erp_bi_dim_customers. Three columns before add_erp_fields(), matching visma_eaccounting_erp_bi_dim_company and upsales_erp_bi_dim_company: OrgId, OrgName, City.

nodes.label: hubspot_erp_bi_dim_customers
nodes.dbt_description: One row per HubSpot company, adapted to the common ERP customer schema. Source is companies, NOT contacts — this dimension is organisation-shaped and HubSpot contacts are people. 44 columns matching fortnox_erp_bi_dim_customers; HubSpot is a CRM, so everything invoice- and delivery-related is typed NULL, as is OrganisationNumber, for which HubSpot has no native property.

nodes.label: shopify_bi_dim_articles
nodes.dbt_description: One row per Shopify product variant. Variant grain so it joins to order rows without fanning out; product-level attributes repeat across a product's variants.

nodes.label: shopify_bi_dim_customers
nodes.dbt_description: One row per Shopify customer — the source-aligned customer dimension Shopify users query directly. Pass-through of shopify_bi_dim_customers_staging with the column list enumerated so a new upstream Shopify field cannot surface here silently.

nodes.label: shopify_bi_fact_order_rows
nodes.dbt_description: One row per line item on a non-cancelled Shopify order. Retains OrderRowId, which the unified erp_bi_fact_order_rows contract has no column for — this is the only layer a consumer can get a line-level key from.

nodes.label: shopify_bi_fact_orders
nodes.dbt_description: One row per Shopify order, cancelled orders excluded, five-year window. Amounts are in the shop's own currency.

nodes.label: shopify_bi_dim_articles_staging
nodes.dbt_description: One row per Shopify product variant. Variant grain, not product grain, because an order line references a variant — a product-grain dimension would fan out when joined to fact_order_rows. Product attributes repeat across a product's variants.

nodes.label: shopify_bi_dim_customers_staging
nodes.dbt_description: One row per Shopify customer. Keys are the raw Shopify `id` with no OrgId prefix — Shopify has no organisation concept and `id` is unique within a shop. Cross-source uniqueness comes from the `-ds_shopify` suffix add_erp_fields() appends downstream. Carries the customer's `default_address` as both the postal and the delivery address.

nodes.label: shopify_bi_fact_order_rows_staging
nodes.dbt_description: One row per line item on a non-cancelled Shopify order. Joins back to shopify_api.orders for order-level context, the same way the Fortnox equivalent joins articles and financial_years. PriceBeforeDiscount strips VAT when the order is stored VAT-inclusive; Discount is a line-level amount, never a percentage.

nodes.label: shopify_bi_fact_orders_staging
nodes.dbt_description: One row per Shopify order, excluding orders cancelled in Shopify (`cancelled_at` set) and orders older than five years. The five-year window mirrors the same filter in fortnox_bi_fact_orders_staging. Amounts are in the shop's own currency, so no FX conversion is applied.

nodes.label: shopify_erp_bi_dim_articles
nodes.dbt_description: Shopify product variants adapted to the common ERP article schema. 10 columns matching fortnox_erp_bi_dim_articles. PurchasePrice is NULL — Shopify exposes no cost price on the REST product resource.

nodes.label: shopify_erp_bi_dim_customers
nodes.dbt_description: Shopify customers adapted to the common ERP customer schema. 44 columns matching fortnox_erp_bi_dim_customers; the columns Shopify has no equivalent for are typed NULL.

nodes.label: shopify_erp_bi_fact_order_rows
nodes.dbt_description: Shopify order lines adapted to the common ERP order-row schema. 28 columns matching fortnox_erp_bi_fact_order_rows. Note that favrit_erp_bi_fact_order_rows emits 30 columns in a different order — that divergence is pre-existing and is not resolved here.

nodes.label: shopify_erp_bi_fact_orders
nodes.dbt_description: Shopify orders adapted to the common ERP order schema. 49 columns matching fortnox_erp_bi_fact_orders. CurrencyRate is 1.0 because Shopify amounts are already in shop currency, which makes the amount columns comparable across sources.
